text.en: Formal nouns (*keishiki meishi*) are a subclass of nouns with weak independence that are placed after verbs or adnominals to form noun phrases, and they are sometimes called 'noun particles' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--formal-nouns-have-weak-independence-are-placed-after⟧. They occur in short and long forms ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--formal-nouns-are-nouns-with-weak-independence-that⟧. Satō (2008a) drew a terminological distinction between complementizers, which he called *meishikaji* 'nominalizers', and the head nouns of relative clauses, which he reserved the label *keishiki-meishi* 'formal nouns' for ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--sat-2008a-distinguished-complementizers-from-formal-nouns-calling⟧. Among the items that function as nominalizers are *ruwe*, *siri*, *hawe*, and *pe* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-siri-hawe-and-pe-function-as-nominalizers⟧. Tamura (1988a) characterizes *takup* as an intermediate category between nouns, noun particles, adverbial particles, and suffixes ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--tamura-1988a-characterizes-takup-as-an-intermediate-category⟧.
text.ja: 形式名詞（*keishiki meishi*）は、自立性が弱く、動詞や連体詞の後ろに置かれて名詞句を形成する名詞の下位類であり、名助詞と呼ばれることもある⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--formal-nouns-have-weak-independence-are-placed-after⟧。形式名詞には短形と長形がある⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--formal-nouns-are-nouns-with-weak-independence-that⟧。佐藤（2008a）は補文標識を「名詞化辞」（*meishikaji*）、関係節の主要部となる名詞を「形式名詞」（*keishiki-meishi*）と呼んで明確に区別した⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--sat-2008a-distinguished-complementizers-from-formal-nouns-calling⟧。名詞化辞として機能する項目には*ruwe*、*siri*、*hawe*、*pe*が含まれる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-siri-hawe-and-pe-function-as-nominalizers⟧。田村（1988a）は*takup*を「名詞」「名助詞」「副助詞」「接尾辞」の中間的存在としている⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--tamura-1988a-characterizes-takup-as-an-intermediate-category⟧。

text.en: The inventory of representative formal nouns includes *p* ~ *pe* 'thing', *hi* 'matter, thing, time, place', *hike* 'direction of ~', *katu* 'manner, state', *uske* 'place', *usi*(*ke*) 'time, place', *kur* 'person', and *utar* '-plural' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--representative-formal-nouns-include-p-pe-thing-hi⟧. While *usi* is widely used across dialects as the formal noun meaning 'place', *uske* is also commonly used in the Saru, Chitose, and Shizunai dialects ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--while-usi-is-widely-used-as-a-formal⟧.
text.ja: 代表的な形式名詞の目録には、*p*〜*pe*「もの」、*hi*「こと・もの・時・ところ」、*hike*「〜の方向」、*katu*「様子・状態」、*uske*「ところ」、*usi*（*ke*）「時・ところ」、*kur*「人」、*utar*「〜たち」などが含まれる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--representative-formal-nouns-include-p-pe-thing-hi⟧。「ところ」を表す形式名詞としては*usi*が広く使われるが、沙流・千歳・静内方言では*uske*もよく使われる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--while-usi-is-widely-used-as-a-formal⟧。

text.en: Complete clauses can only modify a restricted set of semantically bleached formal nouns—including *uske*, *usi*, *hi*, *hike*, *ruwe*, *hawe*, *siri*, and *humi*—to form noun phrases ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--complete-clauses-modify-restricted-formal-nouns⟧. In Hokkaido dialects, a verb phrase can be followed by the formal nouns *hi* and *pe* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-hokkaido-dialects-a-verb-phrase-can-be⟧. Pronouns and formal nouns do not take person affixes ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--pronouns-and-formal-nouns-do-not-take-person⟧. The formal nouns *p* ~ *pe* and *hi* nominalize the entire preceding verb phrase rather than merely attaching to the immediately preceding element, and should therefore be considered clitics rather than affixes ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-nouns-p-pe-and-hi-nominalize⟧. The formal noun *hi* can only be modified by a verb phrase, *p* can be modified by a verb phrase or a prenominal but not by a noun phrase, and *utar* can be modified by verb phrases, noun phrases, or prenominals ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hi-can-only-be-modified⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--verb-phrases-and-adnominals-mainly-precede-formal-nouns⟧. Formal nouns are more concrete in meaning than nominalizers but have low independence; like regular nouns they can be modified by relative clauses, but usually cannot occur alone ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--formal-nouns-keishiki-meishi-are-nouns-with-more⟧. The formal noun *kur* has low syntactic independence and cannot be used alone, requiring a preceding verb or adnominal ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--because-kur-is-a-formal-noun-with-low⟧. The item *takup* possesses properties close to a formal noun, as evidenced by its affiliative form *takupi* matching nominal affiliative morphology ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--takup-possesses-properties-close-to-a-formal-noun⟧, though *takup* cannot follow an adverbial phrase, rendering combinations such as **ukouturuke ta takup* impossible ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--takup-cannot-follow-an-adverbial-phrase-rendering-combinations⟧. When attached to a verb phrase, *patek* is typically verbalized with *ki* 'do', whereas *takup* is frequently verbalized with *ne* 'be' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--when-attached-to-a-verb-phrase-patek-is⟧.
text.ja: 完結文が修飾して名詞句を構成できる名詞は、*uske*、*usi*、*hi*、*hike*、*ruwe*、*hawe*、*siri*、*humi*を含む意味の希薄化した一部の形式名詞に限られる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--complete-clauses-modify-restricted-formal-nouns⟧。北海道方言において、動詞句は形式名詞*hi*および*pe*を後続させることができる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-hokkaido-dialects-a-verb-phrase-can-be⟧。代名詞と形式名詞には人称接辞が付加されない⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--pronouns-and-formal-nouns-do-not-take-person⟧。形式名詞*p*〜*pe*や*hi*は直前の要素だけでなく先行する動詞句全体を名詞化するため、接辞ではなく接語と見なされるべきである⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-nouns-p-pe-and-hi-nominalize⟧。形式名詞*hi*は動詞句によってのみ修飾され、*p*は動詞句または連体詞によって修飾されるが名詞句では修飾されず、*utar*は動詞句・名詞句・連体詞のいずれによっても修飾されうる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hi-can-only-be-modified⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--verb-phrases-and-adnominals-mainly-precede-formal-nouns⟧。形式名詞は名詞化辞よりも具体的な意味を持つが独立性が低く、普通の名詞と同様に関係節化を受けるものの、通常は単独で現れることができない⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--formal-nouns-keishiki-meishi-are-nouns-with-more⟧。形式名詞*kur*は統語的独立性が低く、単独で用いられることがなく、必ず前に動詞や連体詞を取る⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--because-kur-is-a-formal-noun-with-low⟧。*takup*は名詞の所属形と同じ*takupi*という形態を持つことなどから形式名詞に近い性質を持つが⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--takup-possesses-properties-close-to-a-formal-noun⟧、副詞句の後ろに置くことができず、**ukouturuke ta takup*のような言い方はできない⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--takup-cannot-follow-an-adverbial-phrase-rendering-combinations⟧。動詞句に後続した場合、*patek*は*ki*で動詞句化するが、*takup*は*ne*で行うことが多い⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--when-attached-to-a-verb-phrase-patek-is⟧。

text.en: The formal noun meaning 'thing' surfaces as *p* after vowels and *pe* after consonants ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-takes-the-form-pe-after⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-meaning-thing-surfaces-as-p⟧. *Ruwe* and *pe* are semantically neutral dummy nominalizers ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-and-pe-are-semantically-neutral-dummy-nominalizers⟧. As a nominalizer, *ruwe* may only refer to abstract matters, whereas *pe* may in other contexts refer to concrete things or impolitely to persons ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--as-a-nominalizer-ruwe-may-only-refer-to⟧. The formal noun *pe* can mean either 'thing' or 'person', but when applied to humans rather than *kur*, it often carries a derogatory connotation ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-pe-can-mean-either-thing⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-p-pe-can-be-applied⟧. The formal nouns *p* ~ *pe* can also be used as conjunctional particles to connect clauses without serving as an argument of the subsequent clause ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-nouns-p-pe-can-be-used⟧. The expression *pe ne* 'it is the case that' is often used in expressions loaded with strong emotion ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-expression-pe-ne-it-is-the-case⟧.
text.ja: 「もの」を意味する形式名詞は母音の後では*p*、子音の後では*pe*という形をとる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-takes-the-form-pe-after⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-meaning-thing-surfaces-as-p⟧。*ruwe*と*pe*は意味的に中立なダミー名詞化辞である⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-and-pe-are-semantically-neutral-dummy-nominalizers⟧。名詞化辞として*ruwe*は抽象的な事柄にのみ言及できるが、*pe*は他の文脈において具体的な事物や（不作法ながら）人物にも言及しうる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--as-a-nominalizer-ruwe-may-only-refer-to⟧。形式名詞*pe*は「物」「者」どちらの意味にもなるが、人間に対して*kur*ではなく*pe*を使うと、あまり良い意味ではないことが多い⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-pe-can-mean-either-thing⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-p-pe-can-be-applied⟧。形式名詞*p*〜*pe*は、後続節の項にならずに節を接続する接続助詞として使われることもある⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-nouns-p-pe-can-be-used⟧。*pe ne*「ものだ」という表現は、強い感情を込めた表現で使われることが多い⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-expression-pe-ne-it-is-the-case⟧。

text.en: The formal nouns used in sentence-final phrases are basically the four items *ruwe*, *siri*, *hawe*, and *humi* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-nouns-used-in-sentence-final-phrases⟧. When used as formal nouns in their affiliative forms, *ruwe* means 'fact/that', *siri* means 'visible appearance', *hawe* means 'voice', and *humi* means 'sound/(non-visual sensory) feeling', and they function to form a noun phrase from a completed sentence ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--when-ruwe-siri-hawe-and-humi-are-used⟧. Etymologically, these are the affiliative forms of the common nouns *ru* 'path, track', *sir* 'appearance, weather, land', *haw* 'voice', and *hum* 'sound, feeling', respectively ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--etymologically-the-formal-nouns-ruwe-siri-hawe-and⟧. In many dialects sentence-final phrases are formed with the possessed forms *ruwe* and *hawe*, but in the Tokachi dialect the concept forms *ru* and *haw* are used instead ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-many-dialects-sentence-final-phrases-are-formed⟧. Chitose dialect *siri* corresponds to Tokachi dialect *sir*, and Chitose dialect *ruwe* corresponds to Tokachi dialect *ru* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--chitose-dialect-siri-corresponds-to-tokachi-dialect-sir⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--chitose-dialect-ruwe-corresponds-to-tokachi-dialect-ru⟧. Nouns that can serve as complementizers are restricted to a subset of formal nouns, primarily *hi*, *katu*, *p* ~ *pe*, *uske*, *usi*, *ruwe*, *siri*, *hawe*, and *humi* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--nouns-that-can-serve-as-complementizers-in-ainu⟧; formal nouns with abstract meanings can function as complementizers ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--formal-nouns-with-abstract-meanings-can-function-as⟧. The complementizer *uske* 'place' is used mainly in the Saru, Chitose, and Shizunai dialects, while *usi* 'place' is used across all of Hokkaido including those regions ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-complementizer-uske-place-is-used-mainly-in⟧. The sentence-final phrase uses of *ruwe*, *siri*, *hawe*, and *humi* can be regarded as one type of complementizer use ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-sentence-final-phrase-uses-of-ruwe-siri⟧. Noun phrases headed by *hi* 'time/place', *uske* (Saru, Chitose, Shizunai), or *usi*(*ke*) (all Hokkaido) are always treated as grammatical places ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--noun-phrases-headed-by-the-formal-nouns-hi⟧. The formal noun *hi* is treated as 〈location〉 when interpreted as denoting 'time' or 'place' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hi-is-treated-as-location⟧. The bound noun *hi* has minimal concrete meaning, can be translated as 'thing' or 'time', and functions to nominalize a whole clause ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-bound-noun-hi-has-minimal-concrete-meaning⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-morpheme-hi-is-a-nominalizer-used-when⟧. In the Tokachi and Ishikari dialects, the form *ihi* is used alongside *hi*, but it is almost restricted to the expression *ene an ihi* 'that it is thus' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-the-tokachi-and-ishikari-dialects-the-form⟧. Clauses ending in a formal noun plus *ne* construction cannot form a noun phrase except through nominalization with the formal noun *hi* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--clauses-ending-in-a-formal-noun-plus-ne⟧. The generic noun *hi* can function as a subject or a possessor ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-generic-noun-hi-can-function-as-a⟧. In the Tokachi dialect, subordinate clauses formed with the formal nouns *ru*, *haw*, and *hi* can undergo insubordination, but other formal nouns cannot, because insubordination is restricted to forms denoting indirect evidence ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-the-tokachi-dialect-subordinate-clauses-formed-with⟧. The formal noun *hike*, meaning 'one of two or more things' or 'side/direction', can also function like a conjunctional particle setting up the preceding clause as a premise for the situation described in the following clause ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hike-which-means-one-of⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-hike-functions-as-a-formal-noun⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hike-ike-expresses-the-meaning⟧. Satō (2008) proposes that *hike* in the example *a-kouk hike paraparak* might alternatively be interpreted as a formal noun rather than a conjunctive particle ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-the-example-a-kouk-hike-paraparak-hike⟧. The formal noun *usi* means 'place' or 'time', and unlike the locational noun *or* 'place', it can be adnominally modified by a verb phrase in a relative clause construction ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-usi-means-place-or-time⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--unlike-usi-the-locational-noun-or-place-cannot⟧. The combination 'formal noun + *un*' is used as an affirmative response to a polar question ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-combination-formal-noun-un-is-used-as⟧, and nothing—including final particles, formal nouns, and conjunctive particles—ever follows bare formal nouns or 'formal noun + *un*' in sentence-final position ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--nothing-including-final-particles-formal-nouns-and-conjunctive⟧. Polar interrogatives can be formed by ending with *ruwe*, *siri*, *hawe*, or *humi* without a copula ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--polar-interrogatives-yes-no-questions-can-be-formed⟧, while wh-questions using these nominalizers obligatorily place the existential verb *an* after the nominalizer ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-questions-using-the-nominalizers-ruwe-hawe-siri⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--declarative-sentences-end-in-ne-as-in-ruwe⟧. The combination 'formal noun + *an*' is also used to form exclamative sentences, though *an* is not necessarily obligatory in exclamatives as it is in wh-questions ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-nominalizer-construction-with-ruwe-hawe-siri-or⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--while-the-sentence-final-verb-an-is-obligatory⟧. Bare formal nouns used with interrogative words often question the very situation itself rather than asking for specific content ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--when-bare-formal-nouns-ruwe-hawe-etc-are⟧, and bare formal nouns in sentence-final position are also used to express strong emotions such as surprise, admiration, or pain ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--bare-formal-nouns-in-sentence-final-position-are⟧. Exclamatory clauses are expressed by sentence-final phrases ending in *ruwe*, *hawe*, *siri*, or *humi*, and such sentences do not only express admiration but can at times take on an ironic or rhetorical meaning ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--exclamatory-clauses-are-expressed-by-sentence-final-phrases⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--exclamatory-sentences-ending-in-formal-nouns-do-not⟧. Sentence-final phrases using *siri* in particular can express ongoing situations in the present, because *siri* expresses visual information and denotes an action taking place before one's eyes ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--sentence-final-phrases-especially-those-using-siri-express⟧. The combination *ruwe ne* serves as an explanatory construction corresponding to Japanese *no da* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-combination-ruwe-ne-serves-as-an-explanatory⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-ne-has-summarizing-function⟧. One use of *ruwe ne* presents information that the speaker judges the addressee is likely unaware of as new information in the discourse, closely resembling the interpersonal-mood use of Japanese *noda* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--one-use-of-ruwe-ne-presents-information-that⟧, and Hirosawa (2026) asserts that previous research has not described this new-information marking function ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--previous-research-has-not-described-the-new-information⟧. Instances of *ruwe ne* analyzed as having a summarizing function can alternatively be analyzed as presenting new information ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-ne-summarizing-reanalyzed-as-new-info⟧. The comparison 'formal noun + *an*' versus 'formal noun + *ne*' shows that the former has extremely low verbality; when used with interrogative meaning, it is followed only by a small number of elements such as *hi* or the interrogative final particle *ya*, and cannot be connected to a subsequent sentence with a conjunctive particle ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--compared-to-formal-noun-ne-the-verbality-of⟧. The formal noun *humi* can be used in sentence-final expressions to express a sensation such as disgust or horror ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-humi-can-be-used-in⟧, and *humi as* means 'there is a sound' but is also used to mean 'it feels like / there is a feeling that' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--humi-as-means-there-is-a-sound-but⟧. The phrase *siri ka isam* is used to mean 'there is no sign/indication of' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-phrase-siri-ka-isam-is-used-to⟧. The nominalizers *katu* and *siri* are both used after verbs describing a situation or condition ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-nominalizers-katu-and-siri-are-both-used⟧, and *siri* may be used after action verbs to mean the 'way of action' when followed by a descriptive expression ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--siri-may-be-used-after-action-verbs-to⟧; *siri* appears in a number of sentence-final forms ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--siri-appears-in-a-number-of-sentence-final⟧. Tamura (1996) treats one construction as *sir iki*, but Satō proposes *siri iki* in view of the usage of the nominalizer *siri* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--whereas-tamura-1996-treats-this-construction-as-sir⟧. The nominalizers *pokon* and *kotom* indicate that the preceding verb describes how things appear to the speaker, not necessarily how they really are ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-nominalizers-pokon-and-kotom-indicate-that-the⟧, and *pokon* often indicates that the appearance of things is due to pretence on the part of the agent ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--pokon-often-indicates-that-the-appearance-of-things⟧. The phrase *hawe ene an i* takes a speech verb before it and expresses the meaning 'the contents of what was said were as follows' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-phrase-hawe-ene-an-i-takes-a⟧. Satō (2008) proposes that *ukokimatek hawe* can be analyzed as a content clause formed by the nominalizer *hawe* ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ukokimatek-hawe-can-be-analyzed-as-a-content⟧. The adverb *ene* means 'thus, this way' on its own but often combines with a formal noun to form a manner noun clause corresponding to Japanese 'how one should do...' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-adverb-ene-means-thus-this-way-on⟧. In the Saru and Chitose dialects, *orano* and *orowano* are frequently combined with the formal noun *hi* in the forms *hi orano* and *hi orowano*, expressing 'since' or 'after' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-the-saru-and-chitose-dialects-orano-and⟧. The expletives *ko* and *konna* appear primarily after formal nouns such as *ru*, *haw*, *sir*, and *hum*, followed by onomatopoeic/mimetic-based verbs, to adjust meter without adding meaning ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-expletives-ko-and-konna-appear-primarily-after⟧.
text.ja: 文末句として用いられる形式名詞は、基本的に*ruwe*、*siri*、*hawe*、*humi*の4つである⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-nouns-used-in-sentence-final-phrases⟧。所属形の形で形式名詞として使われる時、*ruwe*は「こと・の」、*siri*は「目に見えた様子」、*hawe*は「声」、*humi*は「音・（視覚以外の感覚による）感じ」という意味になり、完結文を受けて名詞句を作る働きをする⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--when-ruwe-siri-hawe-and-humi-are-used⟧。語源的にはこれらはそれぞれ普通名詞*ru*「道・跡」、*sir*「見た目の様子・天候・大地」、*haw*「声」、*hum*「音・感じ」の所属形である⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--etymologically-the-formal-nouns-ruwe-siri-hawe-and⟧。多くの方言では文末句は所属形*ruwe*や*hawe*で構成されるが、十勝方言では概念形*ru*や*haw*が用いられる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-many-dialects-sentence-final-phrases-are-formed⟧。千歳方言の*siri*は十勝方言の*sir*に、千歳方言の*ruwe*は十勝方言の*ru*にそれぞれ対応する⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--chitose-dialect-siri-corresponds-to-tokachi-dialect-sir⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--chitose-dialect-ruwe-corresponds-to-tokachi-dialect-ru⟧。補文標識になる名詞は一部の形式名詞に限られ、おもに*hi*、*katu*、*p*〜*pe*、*uske*、*usi*、*ruwe*、*siri*、*hawe*、*humi*である⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--nouns-that-can-serve-as-complementizers-in-ainu⟧。抽象的な意味の形式名詞が補文標識となることができる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--formal-nouns-with-abstract-meanings-can-function-as⟧。補文標識*uske*「ところ」はおもに沙流・千歳・静内方言で用いられ、*usi*「ところ」は*uske*の使用領域を含む北海道全体で用いられる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-complementizer-uske-place-is-used-mainly-in⟧。*ruwe*、*siri*、*hawe*、*humi*の文末句としての用法も補文標識の一つと考えることができる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-sentence-final-phrase-uses-of-ruwe-siri⟧。形式名詞*hi*「とき・ところ」、*uske*（沙流・千歳・静内方言）、*usi*（*ke*）（北海道全般）を主要部とした名詞句は、常に〈場所〉として扱われる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--noun-phrases-headed-by-the-formal-nouns-hi⟧。形式名詞*hi*は「時」または「場所」と解釈される場合、常に〈位置〉として扱われる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hi-is-treated-as-location⟧。所属名詞*hi*は具体的な意味をほとんど持たず「事・時」のように訳せるが、文全体を名詞化する働きを持つ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-bound-noun-hi-has-minimal-concrete-meaning⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-morpheme-hi-is-a-nominalizer-used-when⟧。十勝方言や石狩方言では*hi*とともに*ihi*という形も使われるが、ほぼ*ene an ihi*という表現に限られる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-the-tokachi-and-ishikari-dialects-the-form⟧。形式名詞＋*ne*型の文末句を含む節は、形式名詞*hi*で名詞句化する以外には名詞句を構成することができない⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--clauses-ending-in-a-formal-noun-plus-ne⟧。形式名詞*hi*は主語や所属者としても機能しうる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-generic-noun-hi-can-function-as-a⟧。十勝方言では形式名詞*ru*、*haw*、*hi*を用いた従属節は脱従属節化が可能であるが、脱従属節化が可能なものは間接証拠を意味するものに限定されるため、それ以外の形式名詞を用いた従属節は脱従属節化できない⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-the-tokachi-dialect-subordinate-clauses-formed-with⟧。「二つ以上あるものの内の一方」または「方・向き」を意味する形式名詞*hike*は、前の文を前提として後ろの文が状況を述べるような場合に接続助詞のように機能することがある⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hike-which-means-one-of⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-hike-functions-as-a-formal-noun⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hike-ike-expresses-the-meaning⟧。佐藤（2008）は*a-kouk hike paraparak*における*hike*を接続助詞ではなく形式名詞と解釈すべきかもしれないと提案している⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-the-example-a-kouk-hike-paraparak-hike⟧。形式名詞*usi*は「ところ・時」を意味し、位置名詞*or*「ところ」と異なり動詞句で連体修飾（関係節化）することができる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-usi-means-place-or-time⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--unlike-usi-the-locational-noun-or-place-cannot⟧。形式名詞＋*un*という言い方は対極疑問文への肯定の返事として用いられ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-combination-formal-noun-un-is-used-as⟧、形式名詞のみの場合と形式名詞＋*un*の後ろには、終助詞・形式名詞・接続助詞を含めて他の要素は何も後続しない⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--nothing-including-final-particles-formal-nouns-and-conjunctive⟧。対極疑問文は*ruwe*、*siri*、*hawe*、*humi*で終わることによって作られ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--polar-interrogatives-yes-no-questions-can-be-formed⟧、これらの名詞化辞を用いた疑問詞疑問文では名詞化辞の後に必ず動詞*an*が置かれる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-questions-using-the-nominalizers-ruwe-hawe-siri⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--declarative-sentences-end-in-ne-as-in-ruwe⟧。「形式名詞＋*an*」という構文は感嘆文を作る場合にも用いられるが、感嘆文では*an*は必ずしも義務的ではない⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-nominalizer-construction-with-ruwe-hawe-siri-or⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--while-the-sentence-final-verb-an-is-obligatory⟧。形式名詞のみの形式は疑問詞とともに使われる場合、内容についての質問をしているというよりはその事態そのものに疑問を呈していることが多く⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--when-bare-formal-nouns-ruwe-hawe-etc-are⟧、文末の形式名詞のみの形式は驚き・感心・苦痛といった強い感情表現にも使われる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--bare-formal-nouns-in-sentence-final-position-are⟧。感嘆文は*ruwe*、*hawe*、*siri*、*humi*で終わる形式で表現され、感心していることばかりを表わすわけではなく時には反語的な意味にもなる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--exclamatory-clauses-are-expressed-by-sentence-final-phrases⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--exclamatory-sentences-ending-in-formal-nouns-do-not⟧。特に*siri*を用いることによって現在進行中の状況を表すことができ、*siri*は視覚的情報を表すため文末句として使われると目の前で行われている行為を表して現在進行形のような意味を持つ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--sentence-final-phrases-especially-those-using-siri-express⟧。*ruwe ne*は日本語の「のだ」にあたる説明の形式として機能する⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-combination-ruwe-ne-serves-as-an-explanatory⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-ne-has-summarizing-function⟧。*ruwe ne*の用法の一つに、話し手が聞き手に認識されていないと判断した内容を談話上の新情報として提示する用法があり、日本語の「対人的ムードのノダ」とよく似ている⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--one-use-of-ruwe-ne-presents-information-that⟧。廣澤（2026）は、先行研究では*ruwe ne*の新情報提示の用法については記述されていないと主張している⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--previous-research-has-not-described-the-new-information⟧。統括機能と分析される*ruwe ne*の用例の一部は、新情報提示として再分析できる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-ne-summarizing-reanalyzed-as-new-info⟧。形式名詞＋*an*は形式名詞＋*ne*に比べて動詞句性は非常に低く、疑問の意味で使われている場合には*hi*か疑問の終助詞*ya*など少数の要素しか後続せず、接続助詞で次の文に続けられることもない⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--compared-to-formal-noun-ne-the-verbality-of⟧。形式名詞*humi*は文末表現において「おぞましさ」のような感覚を表現するために用いられることがある⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-humi-can-be-used-in⟧。*humi as*は「音がする」という意味であるが、「〜のような感じがする」という意味でも用いられる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--humi-as-means-there-is-a-sound-but⟧。*siri ka isam*は「気配・兆しがない」という意味で用いられる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-phrase-siri-ka-isam-is-used-to⟧。名詞化辞*katu*と*siri*はいずれも状況や状態を表す動詞の後に用いられ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-nominalizers-katu-and-siri-are-both-used⟧、*siri*は動作動詞の後に用いられて描写的な表現が続く場合に「動作の仕方」を意味することがある⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--siri-may-be-used-after-action-verbs-to⟧。*siri*は多くの文末形式に現れる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--siri-appears-in-a-number-of-sentence-final⟧。田村（1996）では*sir iki*とされているが、佐藤は名詞化辞の用法から考えて*siri iki*とすることを提案している⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--whereas-tamura-1996-treats-this-construction-as-sir⟧。名詞化辞*pokon*と*kotom*は先行する動詞が事物が話し手にどのように見えるかを表し必ずしも実際のありようではないことを示し⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-nominalizers-pokon-and-kotom-indicate-that-the⟧、*pokon*は事物の現れが動作主の見せかけによるものであることをしばしば示す⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--pokon-often-indicates-that-the-appearance-of-things⟧。*hawe ene an i*は前に発言動詞を取って「言った内容は次のようであった」という意味を表す⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-phrase-hawe-ene-an-i-takes-a⟧。佐藤（2008）は*ukokimatek hawe*を名詞化辞*hawe*による内容節と考えることを提案している⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ukokimatek-hawe-can-be-analyzed-as-a-content⟧。副詞*ene*は単独で「こう・このように」という意味を表すが、形式名詞を後ろに伴って日本語の「どう〜したらよいか」に相当する様態の名詞節を作る働きをすることが多い⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-adverb-ene-means-thus-this-way-on⟧。沙流方言や千歳方言では形式名詞*hi*と組み合わせて*hi orano*、*hi orowano*のような形で「〜から」「〜以来」という意味を表すことが多い⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--in-the-saru-and-chitose-dialects-orano-and⟧。虚辞の*ko*や*konna*は主に*ru*、*haw*、*sir*、*hum*といった形式名詞の後に現れ、擬声語・擬態語を語根にした動詞が続く常套句を形成し、意味を付加せず音律を整える⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-expletives-ko-and-konna-appear-primarily-after⟧。

text.en: The noun *kur* means 'man, human being' and is synchronically not used as an endonym by the Ainu ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-kur-means-man-human-being-and⟧; it is mainly used for men ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-kur-means-person-but-is-mainly⟧. *Kur* functions as a formal noun meaning 'person' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-kur-functions-as-a-formal-noun⟧, and because it has low syntactic independence it cannot be used alone and must be preceded by a verb or an adnominal ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--because-kur-is-a-formal-noun-with-low⟧. The suffix *-kur*, related to the noun *kuru* 'person', extensively derives nominal expressions from phrases and clauses, forming both idiomatic expressions and structures corresponding to English relative clauses headed by 'person' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-suffix-kur-related-to-the-noun-kuru⟧.
text.ja: 名詞*kur*は「男・人間」を意味し、共時的にはアイヌの自称詞としては用いられない⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-kur-means-man-human-being-and⟧。*kur*は主に男性に対して用いられる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-kur-means-person-but-is-mainly⟧。*kur*は「人」を意味する形式名詞として機能するが⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-kur-functions-as-a-formal-noun⟧、統語的独立性が低いため単独で用いられることがなく、必ず前に動詞や連体詞を取る⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--because-kur-is-a-formal-noun-with-low⟧。接尾辞*-kur*（名詞*kuru*「人」に関連）は、句や節から名詞表現を広く派生し、慣用的な形式や英語の「person」を主要部とする関係節に相当する表現を形成する⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-suffix-kur-related-to-the-noun-kuru⟧。

text.en: The formal noun *ruwe* is used to state a fact with certainty ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-ruwe-is-used-to-state⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-ruwe-is-used-when-expressing⟧, and Hirosawa (2026) proposes that it references sensory information or knowledge that the speaker has processed internally ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-references-internally-processed-knowledge⟧. There is, however, a disagreement about its evidential scope: Hirosawa (2026) asserts that *ruwe* can express direct experience or direct evidence ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-expresses-direct-evidence⟧, while another position reported by Hirosawa (2026) holds that *ruwe* is restricted to matters indirectly recognized through comprehension ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-expresses-only-indirect-evidence⟧. According to Tang (2020), in first-person uses of evidential formal nouns, *ruwe* functions to explain matters experienced by the speaker ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--according-to-tang-2020-in-first-person-uses⟧. Hirosawa (2026) notes that *hawe* and *ruwe* can alternate in virtually identical sentences, suggesting that *ruwe* originally refers to information sources obtained through the five senses ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--hawe-and-ruwe-can-alternate-in-virtually-identical⟧. The formal noun *humi* indicates subjective judgment based on perception ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-humi-indicates-subjective-judgment-based⟧. The formal noun *hawe* is used to state hearsay or report what was heard ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hawe-is-used-to-state⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--hawe-exists-as-an-independent-noun-meaning-voice⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--hawe-forms-part-of-sentence-final-forms-where⟧; *hawe* exists as an independent noun meaning 'voice', and as a nominalizer it may only refer to something heard or said ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--hawe-exists-as-an-independent-noun-meaning-voice⟧. *Siri* originally means 'appearance' and as a nominalizer may only refer to something that can be seen ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--siri-originally-means-appearance-and-as-a-nominalizer⟧; it is used to state what is seen visually and can also express an adversative sense 'even though / while' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-shiri-is-used-to-state⟧. *Ruwe* forms part of various sentence-final expressions denoting question or assertion ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-forms-part-of-various-sentence-final-expressions⟧, and the formal noun *ruwe* can be placed clause-finally to form a polite interrogative sentence ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-an-abstract-noun-meaning-matter-fact-functions⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-ruwe-expresses-abstract-matter-fact⟧. The main nominalizers used in interrogatives are *ruwe*, *hawe*, *siri*, and *humi*, which are the affiliative forms of the nouns *ru* 'trace', *haw* 'voice', *sir* 'appearance', and *hum* 'sound' respectively ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-main-nominalizers-used-in-interrogatives-are-ruwe⟧.
text.ja: 形式名詞*ruwe*は事実について確説するために用いられ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-ruwe-is-used-to-state⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-ruwe-is-used-when-expressing⟧、廣澤（2026）は*ruwe*が話者の内的に処理した知覚情報や知識を参照すると提案している⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-references-internally-processed-knowledge⟧。ただし証拠性の範囲については見解が分かれており、廣澤（2026）は*ruwe*が直接体験や直接証拠を表すことができると主張する一方⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-expresses-direct-evidence⟧、廣澤（2026）が報告する別の立場では*ruwe*は理解力を介して間接的に認識される事柄にのみ用いられるとされる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-expresses-only-indirect-evidence⟧。唐（2020）によれば、証拠性形式名詞の一人称での用例において*ruwe*には話し手が自分の経験したことに関する説明を行う機能がある⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--according-to-tang-2020-in-first-person-uses⟧。廣澤（2026）は、ほとんど同じ文で*hawe*と*ruwe*が交替する例が見られ、*ruwe*はもともと五感から得た情報源を参照していると考えられると述べている⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--hawe-and-ruwe-can-alternate-in-virtually-identical⟧。形式名詞*humi*は主観的な判断を示す⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-humi-indicates-subjective-judgment-based⟧。形式名詞*hawe*は聞いたことについて述べるために用いられ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-hawe-is-used-to-state⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--hawe-forms-part-of-sentence-final-forms-where⟧、「声」を意味する名詞としても存在し、名詞化辞としては聞かれたことや発言されたことにのみ言及できる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--hawe-exists-as-an-independent-noun-meaning-voice⟧。*siri*は本来「外見・様子」を意味し、名詞化辞としては目に見えるものにのみ言及でき⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--siri-originally-means-appearance-and-as-a-nominalizer⟧、目で見ている様子について述べるとともに「……のに」という逆接の意味を表すこともある⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-shiri-is-used-to-state⟧。*ruwe*は疑問や断定を表す様々な文末表現の一部を成し⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-forms-part-of-various-sentence-final-expressions⟧、文末に置かれて丁寧な疑問文を作る用法もある⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--ruwe-an-abstract-noun-meaning-matter-fact-functions⟧⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-formal-noun-ruwe-expresses-abstract-matter-fact⟧。疑問文に用いられる主な名詞化辞は*ruwe*、*hawe*、*siri*、*humi*であり、それぞれ名詞*ru*「跡」、*haw*「声」、*sir*「様子」、*hum*「音」の所属形である⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-main-nominalizers-used-in-interrogatives-are-ruwe⟧。

text.en: The possessed forms *ruwe*, *hawe*, *siri*, and *humi* are common nouns that grammaticalized to lose part of their original lexical meaning and function like formal nouns in sentence-final phrases ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-possessed-forms-ruwe-hawe-siri-and-humi⟧. Etymologically, they are the affiliative forms of the common nouns *ru* 'path, track', *sir* 'appearance, weather, land', *haw* 'voice', and *hum* 'sound, feeling', respectively ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--etymologically-the-formal-nouns-ruwe-siri-hawe-and⟧. Hirosawa (2026) proposes that the evidential formal noun *ruwe* derives from the possessed (affiliative) form of the common noun *ru* 'road, track, trace' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-evidential-formal-noun-ruwe-is-thought-to⟧, and reports that according to Chiri (1936), *ruwe* is the concrete form of the noun *ru* 'road/track' and shifted into a factual marker through meanings such as 'there are traces of...' or 'there is the fact that...' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--according-to-chiri-1936-ruwe-is-the-concrete⟧. The bound nouns *pe*/*p* 'thing/person', *hike* 'side', and *hi*/*i* 'place/time' have developed grammaticalized functions as derivational suffixes and subordinating conjunctions ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-bound-nouns-pe-p-thing-person-hike⟧. The ordinary noun *utar* 'companion, relative' has grammaticalized into a formal noun functioning as a pluralizer ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-ordinary-noun-utar-companion-relative-has-grammaticalized⟧. The noun *katu* means 'manner', 'appearance', or 'state' ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-katu-means-manner-appearance-or-state⟧. The form *sittapan*, which likely arose from the conceptual form of the formal noun *sir* combining with *tapan* (*sir*+*tapan* > *sittapan*), is particularly characteristic of the Ishikari dialect ⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-form-sittapan-which-likely-arose-from-the⟧.
text.ja: 所属形*ruwe*、*hawe*、*siri*、*humi*は普通名詞だが文法化によって本来の意味の一部を失い、文末句中で形式名詞のような使われ方をする⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-possessed-forms-ruwe-hawe-siri-and-humi⟧。語源的にはこれらはそれぞれ普通名詞*ru*「道・跡」、*sir*「見た目の様子・天候・大地」、*haw*「声」、*hum*「音・感じ」の所属形である⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--etymologically-the-formal-nouns-ruwe-siri-hawe-and⟧。廣澤（2026）は証拠性形式名詞*ruwe*が普通名詞*ru*「道・跡」の所属形に由来すると提案し⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-evidential-formal-noun-ruwe-is-thought-to⟧、知里（1936）によれば*ruwe*は「路」等を意味する名詞*ru*の具体形であり「何々の痕跡がある」「何々の事実がある」のように事実法に転じていったと考えられると報告している⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--according-to-chiri-1936-ruwe-is-the-concrete⟧。所属名詞*pe*/*p*「もの・人」、*hike*「方」、*hi*/*i*「所・時」は文法化し、派生接尾辞および従属接続詞としての用法を発達させている⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-bound-nouns-pe-p-thing-person-hike⟧。普通名詞*utar*「仲間・親族」は文法化を経て複数化辞として機能する形式名詞になったと考えられる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-ordinary-noun-utar-companion-relative-has-grammaticalized⟧。*katu*は「様子」「有様」「状態」を意味する⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-noun-katu-means-manner-appearance-or-state⟧。形式名詞*sir*の概念形が*tapan*と結合して*sir*+*tapan* > *sittapan*となったと思われる形が、特に石狩方言に特徴的に見られる⟦claim:nominal/formal-defective-nouns--the-form-sittapan-which-likely-arose-from-the⟧。
